question:
Requirement:

We get data having filenames in a specific format which implies which month's data it is (e.g. retailername20230701), we need to make it incremental such that if there is any update made in the source for any of the historical files then that particular file's data should be fully deleted and the data based on the latest load_timestamp should be inserted and any new files will just be processed (i.e. appended as-is).

Note: There is no unique_key for the dataset, it is very uncertain to predict which column's data will change.

sample_table:

name file_name load_timestamp
Mark abc20231201 2023-12-01 09:46:48.021448 UTC
Antony xyz20231203 2023-12-03 10:26:12.021338 UTC
Messi abc20231201 2023-12-01 09:46:48.021448 UTC

Note: If data is updated for the existing filename, it should take the filename and data in it according to the latest load_timestamp and delete the old file records completely. (e.g. Mark should be replaced with Jack)

Name file_name load_timestamp
Jack abc20231201 2024-01-02 10:16:28.041229 UTC
Messi abc20231201 2024-01-02 10:16:28.041229 UTC

Expected Result:

Name file_name load_timestamp
Antony xyz20231203 2023-12-03 10:26:12.021338 UTC
Jack abc20231201 2024-01-02 10:16:28.041229 UTC
Messi abc20231201 2024-01-02 10:16:28.041229 UTC

I have referred this doc and implemented the below code:

{{
    config(
        materialized='incremental',
        partition_by = {'field': 'load_timestamp','data_type': 'timestamp'},
        incremental_strategy= 'insert_overwrite'
    )
}}

select * from sample_table

{% if is_incremental() %}

  -- this filter will only be applied on an incremental run
  -- (uses > to include records whose timestamp occurred since the last run of this model)

  where load_timestamp >= (select max(load_timestamp) from {{ this }})

{% endif %}

I did not get the expected result using the above code and I'm not sure how to modify the code to pass the file_name to delete the corresponding old records & insert the records based on the latest load_timestamp. Can somebody help me to resolve this?
title: Incremental logic on DBT BigQuery using insert_overwrite
answer:
Have you tried partitioning by file_name instead of the load_timestamp?

  partition_by = {'field': 'file_name', 'data_type': 'string'}

This approach will isolate records for each file_name then you can write a query to get the MAX(load_timestamp) of each file so you can filter out later dates in your main SELECT query, although this method keeps historical records instead of deleting them. It's just a habit of mine to keep change-logs for back tracking or troubleshooting purposes.

The MERGE suggestion by @Chiến Lê is also a good option to manage complex scenarios as this will allow more control over updates.
